title: Zebrafish automatic monitoring system for conditioning and behavioral analysis

title: Zebrafish behavior feature recognition using three-dimensional tracking and machine learning
primary_relevance: zebrafish unsupervised ML prior art; temporal-scale precedent
novelty_consequence: Cannot claim ML or unsupervised behavioral feature recognition is new in zebrafish.
notes: Direct precedent for PCA followed by unsupervised clustering of 3D trajectory features. Control extraction verified 2026-08-23: no fish-level held-out split, fish-identity probe, session-leakage test, or speed-matched control was reported in the study methods. Tracking QC was explicit: EthoVision tracks were smoothed, checked for missing samples/reflection clusters/rogue points, and missing values were interpolated before analysis.

novelty_consequence: Detailed zebrafish pose estimation is established and can support a strong non-SSL baseline.

title: ContrastivePose: A contrastive learning approach for self-supervised feature engineering for pose estimation and behavioral classification of interacting animals
primary_relevance: self-supervised pose representation precedent; handcrafted-feature comparison
novelty_consequence: Cannot claim that SSL-vs-handcrafted comparison in animal behavior is itself novel.
notes: Closest conceptual precedent for learning features from pose rather than manually engineering them. Control extraction verified 2026-08-23: ContrastivePose reports downstream supervised classification on pose datasets, but the paper does not report a project-style held-out-subject split, explicit subject-identity leakage probe, session-leakage control, speed-matched analysis, or tracking-artifact QC analysis.

title: Technical Report: Masked Skeleton Sequence Modeling for Learning Larval Zebrafish Behavior Latent Embeddings
segmentation_scale: high-frame-rate skeleton sequences divided into temporal slices
primary_relevance: direct zebrafish SSL; pose-sequence SSL; masked-modeling candidate
novelty_consequence: Direct zebrafish SSL already exists; project novelty must come from matched comparison and validity controls.
evidence_status: targeted deep read/project synthesis; control fields verified 2026-08-23
notes: Strongest direct novelty-boundary paper for the current study. Control extraction verified 2026-08-23: the technical report shows reconstruction on a validation set but does not specify that validation fish are held out by animal. It does not report fish-identity, session, speed, or tracking-artifact nuisance controls. The report notes that masked reconstruction may recover failed pose coordinates, but this is not an explicit tracking-QC confound test.

title: Animal behavioral analysis and neural encoding with transformer-based self-supervised pretraining
unsupervised_behavioral_discovery: downstream behavioral analysis; not a direct match to proposed discovery comparison
handcrafted_comparison: multiple baselines reported in project synthesis
primary_relevance: modern behavioral video SSL; objective candidate; novelty boundary
novelty_consequence: Animal behavioral video SSL with masked and temporal-contrastive objectives is established.
notes: Useful method precedent if a future direct-video extension is pursued. Control extraction verified 2026-08-23: BEAST explicitly evaluates held-out animals for action segmentation (18 train animals, 5 test animals) and uses entirely held-out videos for pose-estimation test frames. It does not report an explicit animal-identity prediction probe or speed-matched/speed-dependence control. Pose evaluation includes held-out-video keypoint error, inspection of erroneous jumps, keypoint difficulty analyses, and correction of identified labeling errors. These count as tracking/pose QC, but are not identical to the present project's cluster-artifact nuisance test.

title: Structure of the Zebrafish Locomotor Repertoire Revealed with Unsupervised Behavioral Clustering
primary_relevance: direct zebrafish unsupervised repertoire discovery; bout-level precedent
novelty_consequence: Cannot claim unsupervised behavioral repertoire discovery has not been done in zebrafish.
notes: Reported 13 basic swim types and hierarchical structure across tail movements and bout sequences. Exact canonical citation should be synced from papers.bib when added. Control extraction verified 2026-08-23: Marques et al. pool millions of naturally segmented bouts across fish/contexts for unsupervised clustering. The paper does not report a project-style held-out-fish evaluation, fish-identity leakage probe, session-leakage test, explicit speed-matched control, or a dedicated tracking-artifact enrichment/QC analysis in the discovery pipeline. Bibliographic fields synchronized to canonical Marques et al. (2018) citation.

title: Hierarchical Compression Reveals Sub-Second to Day-Long Structure in Larval Zebrafish Behavior
segmentation_scale: sub-second bouts through long motifs/day-scale organization
primary_relevance: bout-level unsupervised modules; temporal hierarchy; baseline-feature precedent
novelty_consequence: Establishes multi-timescale bout/motif organization in larval zebrafish.
notes: Active bouts described with bout length, mean, SD, total, min and max activity. Control extraction verified 2026-08-23: Ghosh & Rihel analyze repeated day/night and experimental conditions but do not report a held-out-animal split, identity-leakage probe, session-leakage classifier/control, or explicit speed-matching analysis. Tracking/data QC was explicit: ViewPoint acquisition/order errors were discarded, implausible movement values were thresholded using manual/no-animal controls, water-refill periods were excluded, and bubble/sick/dead-larva exclusions were documented.
